newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Ahold Q4 96 profit seen soaring 60 pct.
newsitem.headline: Ahold Q4 96 profit seen soaring 60 pct.

text.p: Profits of Dutch Ahold NV will again be boosted by the consolidation of American supermarket chain Stop & Shop when the group releases its fourth quarter results on Thursday, analysts said.

They expect the global retailer to post a 213 million guilders net profit over the fourth quarter, a 60 percent rise compared to the same period in 1995, while full year net profit is estimated 37 percent higher at 627 million guilders.
"Stop & Shop (S&S) will be the drive behind the surge in profits, as it was in the third quarter," Jurgen Veenker, analyst at MeesPierson said.
Ahold acquired the chain in July 1996 for $2.9 billion, increasing its U.S. sales by some 50 percent to $11.2 billion.
Analysts said cooperation between S&S and the group's other American supermarket chains would contribute to the overall improvement in Ahold's operational margins.

"I estimate U.S. margins at 4.03 percent in the fourth quarter, compared to 3.20 percent in Q4 '95," said Arie Gravendeel of IRIS, adding full year U.S. margins were likely to have risen to 3.15 percent in 1996 from 2.67 percent in 1995.
Margins in the Netherlands were also set to improve, with Gravendeel estimating a rise to 3.2 from 3.05 percent in 1995.

"We continue to see the impact of improved logistics. Ahold said it would pass on a substantial part of these gains to its (Dutch) customers,...but I still count on a nine percent profit growth in Q4, and a ten percent growth over the full year," said ABN Amro analyst Paul Schram. Ahold has said turnover in the Netherlands grew 4.4 percent in 1996 to 15 billion guilders.
"Other Europe" is expected to be among Ahold's strong growth regions, as booming activities in the Czech Republic counterbalance increasing investments in Poland and Spain.
Sales in the rest of Europe amounted to 2.5 billion guilders in 1996, up 32.8 percent from 1995 sales.
Analysts said the Asia/Pacific region was promising but would not have contributed to profit growth in 1996.
"What profit is made in Brazil or Thailand, will be wiped out by the high investments," said Veenker.
Gravendeel said it would take a couple of years before the region would substantially contribute to profit growth.

"I am positive over the way they tackle the region, allying with local partners, sharing risks and taking advantage of their know-how, but it always takes several years for retail expansion to become profitable," Gravendeel said.
1996 Asia Pacific sales amounted to 57.6 million guilders.

Analysts said the stronger dollar would also add to Ahold's spiralling 1996 profit. Ahold said the 1996 average dollar rate (1.69 versus 1.61 in 1995) had positively influenced its 23.3 percent 1996 turnover growth. It said sales growth would have been limited to 20.0 percent at an unchanged dollar.
Schram said he did not expect Ahold to come up with big surprises on Thursday.
"It's part of their policy to be clear about the way things fare, they keep analysts well informed," he said.
Looking forward, Gravendeel said: "They'll say they target continued profit growth as usual,".
-- Christine Lucassen, Amsterdam newsroom +31 20 504 5000
